neighbours.label: an announcing or completing verb (announced, finished, completed, read, visited) right after a sentence-opening deictic time phrase and its subject: 'Last year the company announced', 'Two weeks ago I finished', 'Next year … will announce'; the same clause without the fronted time phrase stays low
fire: Last month the university announced a new scholarship for nursing students.
Two days ago I finished the last chapter of my thesis and sent it off.
This spring we visited my aunt's vineyard in the hills above the town.
Next month the airline will announce three new routes to South America.
Last week the committee completed its review of the housing plan.
This winter I read every novel on the shelf beside my bed.
A few weeks ago the studio announced a sequel to its biggest hit.
Last summer the team finished the bridge four months ahead of schedule.
quiet: The university announced a new scholarship for nursing students.
I finished the last chapter of my thesis and sent it off.
We visited my aunt's vineyard in the hills above the town.
The airline will announce three new routes to South America.
The committee completed its review of the housing plan last week.
I read every novel on the shelf beside my bed this winter.
The studio that made the film announced a sequel to its biggest hit.
The team that built the tunnel finished the bridge ahead of schedule.

notes: Card: ' announced' x3, ' finished' x2, ' reported' x2, ' that', ' news' after 'Two months ago I', 'Last year it', 'This year I', 'This month, we will'. Probes: 'Next year the company will announce' 1.02, 'Last year the company announced' 0.88, 'Three weeks ago I finished' 0.85, 'This summer we visited' 0.70; the same clauses with no time phrase 0.11; time phrase at the end 0.12. Not every verb works: 'Two years ago they sold' 0.19, 'Last night we watched' 0.19, 'On Tuesday she resigned' 0.09, 'In 2015 the museum opened' 0.24, so the label names the verb class too.
